## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The rewrite of `requirement_proven` must be fixed before merge: it now reports a requirement with no criteria as proven, which the base code rejected. The 180 record-handler diffs and the `itemgetter` change showed no behavior change in the reviewed scope, subject to the limits under Not reviewed.

## Changes
The pull request replaces `typing.List`/`typing.Dict` with built-in generics and `log.warn` with `log.warning` across 180 record handlers and `h091_requirements.py`, and switches `by_name` to `operator.itemgetter`. It also rewrites the return expression of `requirement_proven` and adds a one-line `review.txt` at the repository root.

## Critical
- app/handlers/h091_requirements.py:12 — correctness — Return False for empty criteria again — `requirement_proven([])` now returns `True` where the base returned `False`: the sum over no items is `0`, which equals `len(criteria)`. The base's `bool(criteria) and all(...)` guard is gone, and execution continues past the "requirement has no criteria" warning at line 10. — Release review treats a requirement with no criteria as proven, although the description says no behavior change is intended. — Fix: Return `False` inside the `if not criteria:` branch and extend `test_requirement_proof` in `tests/test_handlers.py` with the empty-list case.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
- review.txt:1 — comments — Remove review.txt — The added line says "the refactor is mechanical", but `app/handlers/h091_requirements.py:12` changes the result for empty criteria with `return proven == len(criteria)`. The description does not mention this file. — The repository root gains a file that misdescribes the change to anyone who reads it later.

## Not reviewed
- The 178 diffs for `app/handlers/h002_records.py` through `app/handlers/h179_records.py` were checked by pattern counts against the template of the two read in full (`h000`, `h001`), not read line by line.
- Those pattern counts do not confirm that the handler number in each `log.warning` message matches the removed `log.warn` line in those 178 files.
- The repository declares no minimum Python version (no `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg` or CI configuration), so this review did not determine whether the `list[...]`/`dict[...]` annotations import on every supported interpreter.
